Canadian merchants round each cash purchase to the
nearest nickel. If a hair comb costs $1.02, consumers pay
a dollar. If it costs $1.03, they pay $1.05. Studies have
shown that its a wash; overall, consumers pay no more or
no less then they did when the penny was in circulation.
Bills for retiring the penny have been floating
around Congress for decades. Whether out of nostalgia
or fear of change, lawmakers have been disinclined to
execute a proposed course of action. But the value of
today’s penny is defective. By retiring the penny,
Congress would cut costs at the US Mint while
also giving cashiers some time back at work.
PASSAGE IV
Under the Mediterranean
From the time Honor Frost made her first amateur
underwater dive in the late 1940s, she was committed to
spending as much time as possible exploring. [
A
] She
was, consequently, thrilled to be invited by professional
divers to join the excavation of a first-century Roman
shipwreck in the Mediterranean Sea in 1957. But
what Frost witnessed during that excavation shocked her.
